subject: POC kickoff — sunrise/sunset handoff windows and staggered hands-on blocks
messages:
From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acme-corp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@neptunecloud.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 14:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC kickoff availability across US/EU/APAC

Hi Irene / Stephanie,

Thanks again for walking us through the platform demo yesterday — the team is excited to proceed to a hands-on POC. We need to lock in a set of staggered, repeatable windows so our engineers in Boston, London and Singapore can rotate without big calendar gymnastics. High level asks: 
- 3 hands-on blocks: prompt review, routing/traffic shaping, and a lightweight load run (not full soak).
- Each block should run for ~90 minutes; we want at least 2 repeatable windows so timezone teams can attend one in their day.

Proposed constraints from Acme:
- Boston team: prefers 08:00–12:00 EDT
- London: prefers 13:00–18:00 BST
- Singapore: prefers 09:00–13:00 SGT

Can Redwood suggest a minimal set of staggered start times that (a) give coverage for all three regions, (b) let your ops run a load window without impacting other tenants, and (c) allow a rotating lead on the sessions?

Attachments: sample calendar matrix (we'll share our internal headcounts after you propose windows).

Best,
Emily
Emily Turner
Lead Platform Engineer, Acme Corporation

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff availability across US/EU/APAC

Hi Emily — great to hear the team is ready. I sketched three stagger patterns that satisfy your constraints and keep our Dedicated pool isolation during load windows. Summary below; attached is a PO runbook and a matrix we use to rotate the "lead" role across timezones.

Option A (minimal overlap):
- Window 1 (US lead): 08:30–10:00 EDT (13:30–15:00 BST / 20:30–22:00 SGT)
- Window 2 (EU lead): 15:00–16:30 BST (10:00–11:30 EDT / 22:00–23:30 SGT)
- Window 3 (APAC lead): 10:00–11:30 SGT (03:00–04:30 BST / 22:00–23:30 EDT previous day) — only if Singapore wants a daytime slot for them.

Option B (rotation-friendly, two full repeats):
- Early block: 07:30–09:00 EDT (12:30–14:00 BST / 19:30–21:00 SGT)
- Late block: 14:30–16:00 BST (09:30–11:00 EDT / 21:30–23:00 SGT)
- We can repeat these two blocks on consecutive days to give each region one convenient attendance slot.

Notes / asks for Acme:
- Can you confirm which option you prefer (A = three specialized windows, B = two repeat blocks)?
- How many simultaneous developer endpoints will you bring for routing/load tests (approx. concurrent sessions)?
- Any blackout windows for your internal ops?

Attachments: POC-runbook-v1.pdf, prototype-itinerary.xlsx (calendar matrix).

If that looks reasonable I'll have Dev and Rishi confirm resource limits and recommended batching/kv-cache settings for the load run.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Emily Turner <emily.turner@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff availability across US/EU/APAC

Folks — quick technical note on the load window:
- For a safe, observable run we recommend a 90-minute window with a ramp-up of 10m and ramp-down of 10m. Peak target: 120 concurrent sessions (stateless gen requests) or 60 sessions if you plan to pin KV-cache heavy flows.
- We'll allocate a Dedicated burst pool (isolated) for those 90m windows in Options A/B above. I attached the YAML we use to provision burst capacity and a sample load plan.

Attachment: redwood-loadplan.yaml

Questions for Acme: how realistic is 120 concurrent clients vs 60? If you want to test routing policies (latency/cost trade-offs) we'll need a small set of canonical prompts and expected output checks (we can reuse the prompt set you previewed).

Thanks,
Dev
Principal Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acme-corp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@neptunecloud.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 10:15:00 +0100
Subject: Re: POC kickoff availability across US/EU/APAC

Irene / Dev — thanks for the breakdown. We'll do Option B (two repeat blocks) for the first two days to reduce ops overhead. Confirming headcount:
- Boston: 6 concurrent devs
- London: 8 concurrent devs
- Singapore: 4 concurrent devs (they prefer the later block)

Tim from Neptune (copartner) asked whether Redwood can provide an abbreviated runbook for their SREs to join the routing tests — can we add a one-page "SRE quickstart" to the runbook? Also our legal team asked about data capture during load runs (logs, KV cache policy).

Forwarded message below for context.

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@neptunecloud.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:40:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Integration ops — SRE participation
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acme-corp.com>

We can onboard SREs for the routing tests. Please add a one-pager with:
- ports & firewall expectations (outbound to Redwood 443, no inbound)
- expected hostnames and certificate thumbprints
- brief rollback steps (how to cut traffic)

—Tim

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acme-corp.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 11:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — sunrise/sunset handoff windows and staggered hands-on blocks

Emily — perfect, thanks for the headcount and confirmation on Option B. Action items and next steps: 
1) Redwood to publish the final two-day schedule (Early block / Late block) and shared calendar invites — will send invites by EOD Monday.
2) Dev / Rishi to generate the burst provisioning and the SRE quickstart one-pager (attachment) — ETA Monday noon BST.
3) We'll add a short data-handling appendix to the runbook addressing logs and KV-cache retention to satisfy your legal team.
4) Please fill the attached calendar matrix with blackout windows (if any) and return by Monday.

Attachments: SRE-quickstart-onepager.pdf (draft)

If no objections I will lock the mutual action plan and add a DocuSign link for the non-prod data-sharing addendum.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
